summary.headline: A burst of requests to specific high-value paths (an individual collection object, the exhibitions listing) triggers a Cloudflare bot challenge that isolated, well-paced requests to the same URLs do not — high severity, Review the Cloudflare bot-management rule thresholds specifically scoped to /collection/works/* and /calendar/exhibitions* to confirm they are not so sensitive that a normal crawl cadence (or a single retry after a transient failure) risks triggering a challenge on the site's own core content.

findings.title: A burst of requests to specific high-value paths (an individual collection object, the exhibitions listing) triggers a Cloudflare bot challenge that isolated, well-paced requests to the same URLs do not
findings.evidence: During this audit's bot-vs-browser parity check (three requests to the same URL in quick succession: a browser control plus a retrieval-agent and a training-agent user-agent), /collection/works/157565 and /calendar/exhibitions both returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare challenge page (16 characters of text, the 'Just a moment...' interstitial, a cf-mitigated response header, and a /cdn-cgi/challenge asset reference) -- identically for all three user-agents, which rules out user-agent-based discrimination and points to an IP-reputation or request-pattern trigger instead. robots.txt places no restriction on either path. A separate, single, well-spaced request to the same collection-object URL made minutes later succeeded twice in a row (HTTP 200, full content). The challenge is real and reproducible under a burst pattern, but not a permanent block -- 2 of 15 sampled paths (13%), both among the site's highest-value, most-likely-to-be-bulk-scraped content types (an individual artwork record, an exhibitions index), were affected under burst conditions.

reproduction.command: for i in 1 2 3; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} ' https://www.moma.org/collection/works/157565; done; echo
reproduction.observed: Three rapid requests: some or all return 403 with a Cloudflare challenge page (confirmed live); a single isolated request to the same URL returns 200
reproduction.expected: Consistent 200 responses regardless of request cadence, for content robots.txt already declares open

suggested_action.summary: Review the Cloudflare bot-management rule thresholds specifically scoped to /collection/works/* and /calendar/exhibitions* to confirm they are not so sensitive that a normal crawl cadence (or a single retry after a transient failure) risks triggering a challenge on the site's own core content.
suggested_action.mechanism: A retrieval agent that retries a failed fetch, or that a second, unrelated crawler happens to request the same popular artwork page around the same time, could plausibly reproduce the same burst pattern this audit did -- and receive a challenge page instead of the content, on exactly the pages (individual collection works, current exhibitions) most likely to be cited when someone asks an assistant about a specific piece or what's currently on view.
steps: Check the bot-management rule configuration for these path patterns specifically, since other sampled paths (the homepage, /visit, /about) did not trigger a challenge under the same request pattern.
Confirm the rate/burst threshold is not tighter on these paths than the rest of the site without a specific reason.
suggested_action.verification: The same three-rapid-request pattern used in this audit's own reproduction returns 200 consistently.

findings.title: VisualArtwork markup on collection object pages omits the date, medium, and description already stated in the page's own visible text
findings.evidence: The sampled collection object page (/collection/works/157565) carries a real, well-formed schema.org VisualArtwork node with name, artist (a Person node correctly linked via sameAs to the artist's own page), image, and url. The page's own visible curatorial text states the creation date ('2011'), the medium ('One from a boxed set of six die-cut folios'), and a full descriptive paragraph about the work's technique and concept -- none of which appear in the VisualArtwork node, despite dateCreated, artMedium and description all being standard properties of that type. By contrast, a sampled exhibition page (/calendar/exhibitions/5906) has complete Event/Offer markup (name, startDate, endDate, location, organizer, and an Offer describing admission), showing the site's structured-data investment is real but inconsistent across content templates rather than absent everywhere.

reproduction.observed: The VisualArtwork node contains only @context, @type, url, artist, image, name
reproduction.expected: The same node also carrying dateCreated (2011), artMedium, and description, matching the values already stated in the page's visible text

suggested_action.summary: Extend the VisualArtwork JSON-LD template to include dateCreated, artMedium, and description, sourced from the same collection-record data already rendered as the page's visible curatorial text.
suggested_action.mechanism: An assistant asked about a specific artwork's date or medium currently has to parse unstructured curatorial prose to find it, when the same page's structured data -- which it may prefer to trust as more precise -- states only the artist and title. Since the values are already in the collection record powering the visible page, this is a template-field addition, not new content or research work.
steps: Add dateCreated, artMedium, and description fields to the VisualArtwork JSON-LD generation, mapped from the same collection-record fields already used for the visible object label and curatorial text.
suggested_action.verification: curl -s <any /collection/works/ URL> | grep -o '"dateCreated":"[^"]*"' returns a match.

opportunities.title: Extend the same rich structured-data investment already made for exhibitions and the homepage to the full collection
opportunities.rationale: The homepage (Museum/TouristAttraction/PostalAddress/GeoCoordinates) and exhibition pages (Event/Offer) already show real, well-formed, type-appropriate markup -- the collection object gap this audit found is a template completeness issue on a foundation that already works, not a from-scratch build.
opportunities.mechanism: A consistent, complete VisualArtwork record for every one of MoMA's collection works would let an assistant answer factual questions about specific artworks -- creation date, medium, current exhibition status -- directly and precisely, which is exactly the kind of citable, structured fact this audit's own thesis cares about most for a museum's core content.
steps: Once the dateCreated/artMedium/description fields are added (see the structured-data finding), verify the same fields populate correctly across the collection's other object-page templates, not just the one sampled here.

not_assessed.check: Off-site corroboration and entity ambiguity (freshness-corroboration-audit, checks 4-5)
not_assessed.reason: Not performed in this run to stay within the demonstration's time budget.
not_assessed.impact: Not a meaningful concern for a globally well-known museum, but genuinely not checked.

not_assessed.check: Whether the Cloudflare challenge burst-sensitivity generalizes beyond the two sampled paths
not_assessed.reason: Only 15 pages were sampled; whether other individual collection-object pages (a very large template, likely representing the bulk of the site's true page count) share the same burst-sensitivity could not be confirmed from this sample alone.
not_assessed.impact: The finding is reported at 'partial' prevalence and medium confidence to reflect this; a broader sample across many collection-object pages would give a more precise prevalence figure.
